name: FlowingMenu-TS-TW
title: FlowingMenu
description: A full-screen stacked menu lists links in tall rows divided by thin lines. Hovering a row slides in a white band that endlessly scrolls its label alongside rounded photo chips.
use: A portfolio or studio site wants a dramatic full-screen menu where each link previews imagery.
avoid: Every row needs an image URL, and on touch there is no hover to start the marquee band.
a11y: The links are real anchors with browser focus rings, but the marquee happens only on hover, so keyboard focus shows no preview. (keyboard: partial, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Four tall dark rows stack edge to edge, each centred with a small uppercase white label and divided by thin white rules. On hover a white band covers the row, running large text and pill-shaped photos across it.
behaves: The white band slides in from whichever edge the pointer entered, then scrolls its repeated label and photos sideways without stopping. Leaving the row pushes the band back out the same way.
customise: Items with link, label and image, plus scroll speed and the text, background, band, band-text and border colours are props; the band layout is fixed.
weight: moderate: Every row starts its own endless marquee tween on mount, even while hidden.
demo: Four items labelled Home, Work, About and Contact, with stock interior and portrait photos in the hover bands.
issues: Every row runs its marquee animation from mount, so four hidden loops keep moving all the time.
polishWhy: Bold full-width menu with a slick moving band; the resting screen is only four small labels.
